excluded.reason: Upstream Chromium (Google Gemini auto-browse) UI strings present in Aside's Chromium base; not an Aside-built capability, evidence of upstream pattern only (pattern covered by takeover cluster C19)
Desktop-local named-pipe framing between Node REPL and Electron host; transport trivia with no product relevance for a networked, server-side Quarry

clusters.name: Authenticated agent-to-browser control channel (agent loop outside the browser, routed command bridge)
clusters.description: The agent loop runs outside the browser process and drives it over an authenticated, routed channel: page-level control over a token-gated CDP endpoint, browser-level commands over a separate bridge, with per-turn proof that browser use is enabled.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: the CDP server refuses unauthenticated clients and issues short-lived tokens only after a signed installation challenge; the bridge is routed per (account, profile, mode), cancellable and detects stale connections. Codex CA028 (signed per-turn verification) is the complementary idea.

clusters.mechanism: (1) Browser DevTools server accepts only a bearer token; client GETs /json/challenge, signs it with an installation key, POSTs to /json/auth/session for a short-lived token. (2) Browser-level commands use a WebSocket bridge: register{connectionId, route{accountId,profileId,mode}} then runCommand{id,command,params}/cancelCommand; stale or replaced connections are rejected. (3) Non-standard methods (Aside.*) go through the same send() and are routed to the bridge. Verevon analogue: model-gateway/execution-core sends typed actions to quarry-edge with a BrowserBroker grant (x-browser-authorization) that Quarry validates per action.

verevon.gap: The topology is right (Model proposes, Quarry executes, broker grant validated per action in quarry-edge) but it is not wired end to end: BrowserBroker keeps grants in memory and has no production AcquireGrant caller; the Verevon gateway sends grant_id 'session:{id}' without x-browser-authorization, and the AI-step route lacks x-inference-authorization, so AI-step/AI-loop likely return 401/403 (baseline SRC+INF high).
verevon.strengths: Server-side, plane-separated authority is stronger than a local daemon: grants are org/owner scoped, TTL-bound and checked by the executor, not the model.

clusters.benefit: Unblocks every AI-browser feature: without issued grants and correct gateway headers, users cannot run any agent step in the in-app browser. Keeps the authority model intact (broker issues, Quarry enforces).
clusters.approach: Model Plane: give BrowserBroker a durable store (Postgres) and an AcquireGrant path called by model-gateway when a run starts (scoped to org, owner, session, domain set, TTL). Frontend gateway: forward x-inference-authorization and a real broker grant instead of 'session:{id}'. Add an end-to-end contract test gateway -> model-gateway -> execution-core -> quarry-edge.
dependencies: Control Plane identity for org/owner scope
clusters.risks: Grant scope too broad would widen ACLs; keep grants per run and per domain set, never per user globally. ZDR runs must not persist grants beyond the run.
clusters.rationale: Blocking: shipped pieces in Quarry and execution-core are unreachable from the product until grants are issued and headers forwarded.

clusters.name: Purpose-built browser-level command catalogue with audited tab/window/bookmark management
clusters.description: A small, schema-validated command set for browser state CDP cannot reach (tab groups, notifications, downloads, bookmarks), with read-only passthrough by default and an audit trail of model-initiated changes.

bestInClass.why: q5/q4 SRC: Chrome-API-shaped management capability that logs every model-initiated change with the pre-change state, behind a guarded capability.

clusters.mechanism: Expose a typed allowlist (list/open/close/group tabs, bookmarks CRUD, history queries) instead of raw chrome.*; mutating calls require a capability flag and write an audit row {before, after, turnId}.

verevon.gap: Quarry offers multi-tab per run and immutable step receipts, but there is no user-browser state (bookmarks, history, tab groups) to manage because Quarry sessions are server-side.
verevon.strengths: Step receipts already give an audit trail of every agent action.

clusters.benefit: Low: Verevon's browser is server-hosted, so user bookmark/tab-group management has little value.
clusters.approach: No new build. If user-facing tab organisation in the Verevon browser chrome is wanted later, model it as Application Plane workspace state, not as a Quarry capability.
clusters.risks: Adding mutable user-state APIs to the agent widens blast radius without clear benefit.
clusters.rationale: Designed for a user's desktop browser; does not fit server-side Quarry sessions.

clusters.name: Code-mode browser control: model writes a script against a typed browser runtime (single REPL tool)
clusters.description: Instead of one tool call per action, the model writes JavaScript in a persistent sandboxed REPL with a Playwright-like API, batching several actions and reads per turn; programmatic reads can stay out of the model context. Firecrawl's variant (FA099) runs caller-written code against a live session.

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC: one persistent QuickJS scope per session with a deliberately small surface (page, tabs, snapshot, annotatedScreenshot, fetch) plus runtime lints; Codex CA077/CA054 add the model-visible vs programmatic observation split.

clusters.mechanism: Embed a WASM JS engine (QuickJS) with memory/stack limits and an interrupt deadline; keep one top-level scope per session; inject host functions (page.goto, locator.click, snapshot()) that marshal to typed commands; return only values the script emits (write/emit) to the model while get() results stay in-script. In Verevon the host functions would be thin clients for quarry-edge /step so each call is still grant-checked by Quarry.

verevon.gap: Verevon exposes browser.observe / browser.act as one typed action per model call; no batching, no programmatic post-processing of page data before it reaches the model.

clusters.benefit: Fewer model round-trips and tokens for multi-step tasks (fill a form, paginate, extract a table), lower latency and cost; matches how both reference agents operate. Preserves 'Model proposes, Quarry executes' if each host call is a Quarry step.
clusters.approach: Model Plane sandboxes: run model-written scripts in a QuickJS/V8 isolate inside execution-core with only typed Quarry bindings (observe, act, locator, extract); no network, fs or raw CDP. Every binding call goes to quarry-edge with the run's grant, so Quarry still validates and receipts each action.
clusters.risks: Larger attack surface (model-written code); approvals must happen per Quarry step, not per script, because one script can contain many actions.
clusters.rationale: Material efficiency win, not a blocker; build after C01/C51 are live.

clusters.name: Sandbox hardening for model-written browser code and approval inputs
clusters.description: Model code cannot reach raw CDP or browser handles, cannot import modules, runs under deadlines, and approval-gate inputs are frozen plain data so getters/proxies cannot change what was approved.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: approval inputs are checked to be plain data properties and copied into a frozen object before approval, closing a TOCTOU gap specific to code-mode; Aside AA083 adds non-marshalable host handles.

clusters.mechanism: Host handles are opaque (not structurally clonable); module import/require rejected; per-call deadline interrupt; before any approval, deep-copy arguments verifying own data properties only, freeze, and execute exactly the frozen copy.

verevon.gap: Only relevant if Verevon adopts code-mode (C03). Current typed JSON actions are already plain data.
verevon.strengths: Typed JSON actions over HTTP are inherently immune to getter/proxy tricks.

clusters.benefit: Required safety envelope for C03.
clusters.approach: Implement together with C03 in the Model Plane sandbox: opaque handles, no imports, deadline, freeze-and-copy of every argument that reaches an approval or Quarry call.
clusters.risks: Shipping C03 without this would create approval bypasses.
clusters.rationale: Only together with C03; no standalone value.

clusters.name: Typed backend-agnostic command protocol with per-backend capability discovery
clusters.description: All browser operations are typed commands shared across backends; the runtime tells the model which members each backend supports and discovers optional capabilities at runtime.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: about 85 zod-typed command types shared by in-app, extension, CDP, MCP Apps and cloud backends, with an unsupportedByDefaultIn matrix.

clusters.mechanism: One schema per command (type, payload schema); backends declare a support matrix; a capability discovery call returns supported members; unsupported calls fail with a typed 'capability unavailable' error.

verevon.gap: Capability matrix is enforced fail-closed in Quarry; check that execution-core surfaces driver capabilities to the model (see C06).
verevon.strengths: Typed Rust AgentAction contracts plus fail-closed driver capability gating are on par with Codex.

clusters.approach: Keep; expose the capability set to the planner prompt (C06).
clusters.rationale: Verevon is equal: typed contracts and fail-closed capability gating are shipped.

clusters.name: Capability- and environment-conditional tool docs and policy delivered as data
clusters.description: The documentation and tools the model receives depend on backend capabilities, session kind (main, subagent, headless, incognito) and environment; risky APIs require the model to have read the policy doc first; the server can push updated policy text per request; model-specific prompt overrides.

bestInClass.why: q5/q4 SRC: docs filtered by advertised capability, doc-read enforcement before raw CDP/WebMCP, and server-pushed confirmation policy overriding packaged text without a release.

clusters.mechanism: Build the tool description from a docs index filtered by {backend, capabilities, environment}; track which doc ids were emitted in this context and reject calls to gated APIs until the gate doc was emitted; allow request metadata to replace policy text; re-emit docs after context summarisation. Aside AB088 varies the tool set by session kind.

verevon.gap: Unknown: check whether execution-core's browser tool schema/prompt is generated from Quarry driver capabilities and run kind (ZDR, headless, approval-less), and whether policy text is versioned server-side.

clusters.benefit: Prevents the model from attempting unsupported or forbidden actions (fewer failed steps), lets Verevon change browser policy centrally in the Model Plane without frontend releases, and supports ZDR/headless variants cleanly.
clusters.approach: Model Plane: generate browser tool descriptions from the Quarry capability response plus run attributes; store policy text as versioned config; add 'must have read X' gating for escape hatches (C32).
clusters.risks: Doc drift between policy text and enforcement; enforcement must stay in Quarry/broker, docs are guidance only.
clusters.rationale: Cheap reliability and governance win once the loop is live.

clusters.name: Browsing operating procedure in the system prompt (snapshot-first, verify, efficiency limits)
clusters.description: Concrete rules for web work: read via snapshot, escalate to screenshots only when needed, treat actions as unconfirmed until a fresh observation shows the effect, bounded exploration (one direct URL attempt, one search), and environment stance.

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC: complete procedure including verification and recovery; Codex CA070 (DOC) adds efficiency caps.

clusters.mechanism: Prompt sections: observe -> act -> re-observe to confirm; escalation ladder (AX -> locator -> screenshot -> coordinates); stop rules (no URL-guessing loops, trust one authoritative on-page signal); periodic progress updates and final proof.

verevon.gap: Unknown: inspect the llm_planner.rs prompt for verification and efficiency rules; the LLM planner is also disabled by default (QUARRY_BROWSER_AGENT_LLM unset).

clusters.benefit: Directly improves task success and cost of the browser agent at near-zero engineering cost.
clusters.approach: Model Plane: add a versioned browsing procedure prompt to the planner (observe-act-verify, escalation ladder, stop rules); evaluate with Quarry step receipts.
clusters.risks: Over-long prompts; keep rules short and test-driven.
clusters.rationale: High leverage, small effort.

clusters.name: Surface selection: connector or search before browser, single gated control channel
clusters.description: For semantic tasks the agent must prefer a purpose-built connector/API or web search; the browser is used on explicit intent or as fallback, only through the gated runtime (no side doors such as shell Playwright); an explicitly named browser is a hard constraint.

bestInClass.why: q5/q4 DOC: crisp routing rule (connector first, browser on explicit intent or fallback) plus a no-side-door rule.

clusters.mechanism: Planner routing step: if a linked resource has a connector capability, call it; for public lookups use search; open the browser only on explicit intent or connector failure. All browser control goes through one gated API; other automation tools are hidden from browsing agents.

verevon.gap: Single channel is shipped (UI browser actions are not model-executable; the model uses execution-core tools only). Connector-first routing between Integration Plane provider actions, Quarry search and the browser is unverified: check execution-core tool routing.
verevon.strengths: UI/model action separation is already enforced by an allowlist.

clusters.benefit: Verevon owns an Integration Plane (integration-corev2) with provider actions; routing to it before browser automation is cheaper, more reliable and respects provider OAuth scopes instead of driving UIs.
clusters.approach: Model Plane: add a routing policy in planner/tool selection (connector -> Quarry search/scrape -> browser), recorded in run receipts; keep browser tools unavailable to agents that have a matching connector unless the user asked for the browser.
clusters.risks: Over-eager routing can ignore the user's explicit wish to use the browser; honour explicit intent.
clusters.rationale: Fits Verevon's plane design and reduces risky browsing.

clusters.name: Accessibility-tree observation with stable element refs and diffs
clusters.description: The primary page observation is a compact accessibility-style tree with short element refs (frame-aware), and after each action the model receives a diff instead of a full tree. Firecrawl's interact agent (FA098/FE098, clustered in C51) uses the same @eN-ref pattern.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: refs per element with iframe prefixes (f1e3), shadow DOM traversal, W3C accessible names, scoping and text diffs; Codex CA053/CI080 is equivalent with index targets and revision-keyed diffs.

clusters.mechanism: Inject a script into a CDP isolated world per frame; walk light/shadow DOM and aria-owns; compute role and accessible name; assign refs stored in a per-snapshot WeakMap/symbol; render a compact indented text; keep the previous text per tab and return removed/added/changed lines after actions.

verevon.gap: None material. Verify that deltas are returned to the model by default after each act (baseline says deltas exist in the observation protocol).
verevon.strengths: Quarry binds refs to CDP backend node ids from the native AX tree (stronger than injected-script refs) and discloses frames origin-only.

clusters.approach: Keep; consider Aside-style scoped snapshots (subtree by ref) to cut tokens.
clusters.rationale: Verevon is equal or ahead on the core observation primitive.

clusters.name: Stale-target protection and ref re-resolution
clusters.description: Element refs are valid only for the observation that produced them; actions on stale refs fail loudly (Codex) or the runtime re-finds the same logical control by role, name and ordinal before failing (Aside); coordinate input is refused if the window changed since the screenshot.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: captures keyed by documentKey (main frame + loader id) and AX revision; straddling captures are discarded. Aside AA021 (q4) adds automatic re-resolution.

clusters.mechanism: Key each observation by (frameId, loaderId, axRevision); store per ref a signature {role, name, tag, inputType, ariaLabel, placeholder, nth}; on act: if the node is gone, optionally re-resolve by signature uniquely, else return a typed STALE error telling the model to re-observe.

verevon.gap: Fail-closed is shipped (TARGET_REPAIR_REQUIRED). Missing only the optional Aside-style unique re-resolution by signature, which would save a re-observe round-trip.
verevon.strengths: Fail-closed stale detection with frame-execution-context checks matches Codex.

clusters.approach: Optional: add signature-based unique re-resolution in quarry-runtime before returning TARGET_REPAIR_REQUIRED.
clusters.risks: Re-resolution must refuse ambiguous matches.
clusters.rationale: Equal to Codex; re-resolution is a minor optimisation.

clusters.name: Actionability checks, hit-target verification and trusted input events
clusters.description: Before clicking or typing, wait for attached/visible/enabled/stable, scroll into view, verify that the click point actually hits the target (through shadow roots and cross-process iframes) and report 'covered by X'; deliver real CDP input (isTrusted) with modifiers and platform-aware keyboard synthesis.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: hit-testing across nested and cross-process iframes returning hittable|covered(hitTag)|unpositioned, plus realistic key synthesis bound to an input target token. Aside AA022 (q4) has a clear waitForReady(attached|visible|enabled|stable) with 32 ms stability sampling.

clusters.mechanism: For a target: DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded; poll getContentQuads until stable over two frames; compute centre point; DOM.getNodeForLocation (per frame hop with coordinate transforms) and check that the hit node is the target or its descendant; else error 'covered by <tag>'; then Input.dispatchMouseEvent moved/pressed/released and Input.dispatchKeyEvent with modifiers.

verevon.gap: Quarry's ref-targeted act (execute_native_target_action) resolves the backend node, checks isConnected and then calls element.click() via Runtime.callFunctionOn: a synthetic, non-trusted click with no visibility, stability, scroll or covered-element check (SRC, read in this audit). Only coordinate click_point uses trusted Input.dispatchMouseEvent. Sites that ignore untrusted events or have overlays will silently mis-act.
verevon.strengths: Atomic verify-and-act on backend node ids and frame contexts.

clusters.benefit: Higher action success and fewer silent no-op clicks; honest errors ('covered by cookie banner') let the model recover. Users notice flaky agents immediately.
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane (quarry-browser): implement actionability (attached, visible, enabled, stable), scroll into view, hit-test via DOM.getNodeForLocation including OOPIF hops, then trusted CDP input; keep element.click() only as an explicit fallback. Return typed errors (covered, not_visible, disabled).
clusters.risks: Trusted input on cross-origin iframes needs coordinate transforms; regression risk in existing flows, so ship behind a driver capability first.
clusters.rationale: Core reliability gap in the executor every AI action passes through.

clusters.name: Rich input action set and isolated agent clipboard
clusters.description: AX-index actions include held clicks, drag, typed paste in text/markdown/html, key presses with modifiers, select text, set value and secondary actions (expand/collapse); the agent has its own virtual clipboard so it never touches the user's clipboard.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: page-side bridge replaces navigator.clipboard with a virtual implementation, cleaned at turn end; action set is DOC-backed (q4).

clusters.mechanism: Runtime binding installs a per-page clipboard shim (ClipboardItem blobs, base64 transport) used by paste actions; actions are an enum over AX indices with options {clickCount, duration, modifiers, button}.

verevon.gap: Unknown: check AgentAction variants in contracts.rs for press_key with modifiers, drag, select_text, secondary actions and rich paste; no clipboard support found by grep in Quarry crates.

clusters.benefit: Moderate: rich-editor and spreadsheet tasks need paste/select/keyboard shortcuts; server-side Quarry has no user clipboard to protect, so the isolation aspect matters less.
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane: extend AgentAction with paste{format}, press_key{modifiers}, drag, select_text, perform_secondary_action; per-session virtual clipboard in the page.
clusters.risks: Low.
clusters.rationale: Useful for rich editors; not core.

clusters.name: Post-action settle logic and ambient page-event notes
clusters.description: After an action the runtime waits just long enough (DOM quiet window, same-site request tracking, SPA navigation dwell) instead of fixed sleeps, and surfaces background events (navigated, dialog, popup, download, new tab) to the model as short system lines or a cursor-based event buffer.

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC: concrete constants (350 ms quiet window with <=1% mutation ratio sampled twice, 1.2 s request tracking budget, 300 ms post-settle) and queued ambient notes flushed into the next tool result; Codex CA020 adds a cursor-based CDP event buffer purged on origin change.

clusters.mechanism: After act: wait for DOMContentLoaded (<=2 s), then sample MutationObserver counts every 100 ms until a 350 ms window has <=1% mutation ratio twice; track same-site in-flight requests up to 1.2 s; extra dwell on SPA URL changes. Queue framenavigated/dialog/popup/download events and append them to the next observation.

verevon.gap: Quarry has explicit wait_for actions and fixed waits plus a typed agent-event SSE for the UI, but no adaptive post-action settle was found (grep), and page events are not shown to have been injected into the model's next observation (check observation deltas).
verevon.strengths: Typed event stream with durable replay already exists for the UI.

clusters.benefit: Fewer stale observations and wasted steps; lower latency than fixed sleeps.
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane: add an adaptive settle stage after every act in quarry-browser (mutation quiet window plus request tracking) and attach a bounded 'events since last observation' list to the observation contract; Model Plane renders it into the tool result.
clusters.risks: Long-polling pages (websockets, analytics beacons) need same-site filtering and caps.
clusters.rationale: Reliability and speed gain at moderate cost.

clusters.name: Multi-path input with visual fallback: AX -> DOM node -> coordinates, with set-of-marks screenshots
clusters.description: When refs cannot reach the target (canvas, maps, sliders), the agent can request a screenshot with numbered boxes on interactive elements, act on visible-DOM node ids, or use coordinate actions; guidance restricts coordinates to pixel-only UIs.

bestInClass.why: q4/q3 SRC: annotatedScreenshot draws ref labels so the model can pick by number, and the cua skill is explicitly gated to pixel-only cases; Codex CI082/CA060 offer the same three paths (DOC/SRC).

clusters.mechanism: Take Page.captureScreenshot, overlay boxes for each interactive ref (from the AX snapshot's box model) with the ref label, return PNG plus legend; coordinate actions via Input.dispatchMouseEvent; prompt rule: return to snapshots after a visual action.

verevon.gap: Coordinate actions and visual evidence are shipped. ArtifactKind::ScreenshotAnnotated exists in quarry-core but no producer was found (only parsing in artifact_store.rs:23), so set-of-marks screenshots appear absent (SRC grep, INF). No visible-DOM node-id path.
verevon.strengths: Coordinate actions use trusted CDP input.

clusters.benefit: Lets vision-capable models act reliably on canvas-heavy apps without guessing pixels.
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane: render set-of-marks overlays server-side from the AX snapshot boxes (no page injection), store as ScreenshotAnnotated artifact (skipped or ephemeral under ZDR), expose 'act by mark number' mapped back to the ref.
clusters.risks: Screenshots under ZDR must stay ephemeral; marks must map to refs from the same observation revision.
clusters.rationale: Small build on existing artifact type; improves vision fallback.

clusters.name: Playwright-compatible semantic locators across frames with failure diagnostics
clusters.description: getByRole/Text/Label/Placeholder/TestId, frameLocator, filter/nth chains and waits; cross-origin iframes visible; failed actions return match counts and sample matches.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: full locator algebra plus rich failure diagnostics (counts, samples, ranked selector candidates via elementInfo(x,y)).

clusters.mechanism: Locator = chain of (selector engine, filter, nth); resolve against AX/DOM per frame; strict mode fails on ambiguity with a diagnostic listing the first N candidates with role/name.

verevon.gap: Check whether ambiguous/no-match errors include candidate samples like Codex.
verevon.strengths: Semantic locators with fail-closed ambiguity and explicit OOPIF frame actions are shipped.

clusters.approach: Keep; add candidate samples to ambiguity errors if missing.
clusters.rationale: Equal.

clusters.name: JavaScript dialog handling as controllable objects
clusters.description: alert/confirm/prompt/beforeunload are exposed to the agent as objects it can accept or dismiss instead of hanging the page. Aside auto-accepts dialogs (AA023, clustered in C11) and reports them as ambient notes.

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC: dialogs appear as AX nodes with accept/dismiss/prompt controls; screenshots are declined with guidance while a dialog is open.

clusters.mechanism: Listen to Page.javascriptDialogOpening; expose a pending-dialog node in the observation; Page.handleJavaScriptDialog on explicit agent action.

verevon.gap: None.
verevon.strengths: Never auto-resolved and requires a one-shot approval grant scoped to the exact dialog: stricter than Aside's auto-accept.

clusters.approach: Keep.
clusters.rationale: Verevon is ahead of Aside and equal to Codex.

clusters.name: Agent tab ownership and turn-scoped tab lifecycle
clusters.description: Tabs the agent opens are owned and cleaned up (idle auto-close, turn end) unless marked as a deliverable or handoff; user tabs attached by the agent are borrowed and never closed; agent tabs are grouped and sessions are pinned to profile/window/anchor tab.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: temporary vs persistent tabs, markTab({status: handoff|deliverable}), cleanup on turn end restoring clipboards and detaching debuggers. Aside AA030/AA031 (q4) add owned/borrowed rows and an 'Agent Tabs' group with orphan reconciliation.

clusters.mechanism: session_tabs(sessionId, targetId, ownership owned|borrowed, source, mark) ; on turn/run end: close owned unmarked tabs, release borrowed ones, keep deliverable/handoff tabs; idle sweeper closes after N minutes; reconcile orphans on restart.

verevon.gap: Quarry supports multiple tabs per run, but runs use their own lease, window.open is rewritten to same-tab navigation, and there is no deliverable/handoff marking so the user cannot be left on the result tab.
verevon.strengths: Server-side lease isolation per run.

clusters.benefit: Lets an agent hand the finished page to the user in the Verevon browser (the result stays open as a deliverable).
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane: add tab ownership and mark{deliverable|handoff} to the Quarry session model; Frontend shows marked tabs after the run.
clusters.risks: Tab leaks without idle sweep.
clusters.rationale: Valuable mostly as part of co-browsing (C18).

clusters.name: Co-browsing: agent claims the tab the user is looking at (fail-closed tab claiming)
clusters.description: The agent can list the user's open tabs and claim one for control (without moving it), or act on a tab mentioned in the prompt; claiming requires an exact match of tab id, title and URL, else the agent reports it unavailable. Aside attaches user tabs as 'borrowed' (AA030, C17).

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC/DOC: claimTab returns a controllable tab, unmarked claimed tabs are released at turn end, and mention resolution fails closed on any mismatch.

clusters.mechanism: User tab list from the browser surface -> mention token {browserId, tabId, title, url}; claim validates all three against live state, takes a control lease on that tab, and releases (not closes) it at end of turn.

verevon.gap: The AI run acquires its own Quarry lease; continuity with the user's tab is only via profile_id/start_url. The agent cannot act on the exact page state (form progress, scroll, logged-in session) the user is looking at.

clusters.benefit: This is the product vision ('a built-in browser that users and AI both use'): the user browses, asks the AI to continue on this page, and watches it work. Users notice its absence immediately.
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane: let a Quarry session have one control lease holder at a time (user|agent) with a lease-transfer API; Model Plane: browser_run accepts an existing session/tab id plus a grant scoped to that session; Frontend: 'Ask AI on this tab' passes the mention token. Combine with C19 takeover and C20 presentation.
clusters.risks: Lease races between user input and agent steps; must not widen the user's ACL (the agent inherits only the session's grant); ZDR sessions must stay non-persistent.
clusters.rationale: Central to Verevon's in-app browser vision; absent today.

clusters.name: User takeover, manual handoff and interruption
clusters.description: The user can take over the controlled tab at any time (Take over button, stop/interrupt), the agent stops cleanly and is told the user took over; the agent can request a manual handoff for CAPTCHA/MFA and the tab stays alive for the next turn.

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC: typed user_took_over status, interrupt hooks that stop automation, and a requestManualHandoff command that keeps the cloud tab alive. Aside AB062 (q4) contributes the 'Aside is controlling this tab / Take over' strip; Aside AA061 (INF) notes its daemon does not detect user input.

clusters.mechanism: Session control_mode {agent|human}; UI 'Take over' flips it and cancels in-flight agent steps; every agent /step checks control_mode and returns USER_TOOK_OVER; agent-initiated handoff sets control_mode=human with a reason and resumes on user 'Give back'.

verevon.gap: Control-mode transfer is recorded server-side, but /step does not block the agent while human_takeover is active, and step receipts do not record the initiator (user vs agent).
verevon.strengths: Server-side control-mode record and UI controls exist.

clusters.benefit: Safety and trust: the user can always grab control and the agent provably stops; needed for co-browsing and for CAPTCHA/MFA handoffs (Quarry never bypasses challenges).
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane: enforce control_mode in quarry-edge /step (reject agent steps with typed USER_TOOK_OVER while human), add initiator to receipts, add agent 'request_handoff' action with reason; Model Plane: map USER_TOOK_OVER to a suspended run.
clusters.risks: Race between in-flight step and takeover; use a monotonic control epoch on every step.
clusters.rationale: Small, high-trust fix; prerequisite for co-browsing.

clusters.name: Agent activity presentation: animated cursor, active-tab state, visibility and viewport control
clusters.description: The app animates an agent cursor to each target before the click lands, marks the tab as agent-active, protects it from suspension, and lets the agent work in the background or explicitly show the browser/set the viewport. Aside has no page-level cursor (AA062).

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: every pointer command first moves a host-drawn cursor and waits for arrival acknowledgement (moveSequence) before the click.

clusters.mechanism: Before each pointer action, executor emits {moveSequence, x, y} to the UI; UI animates a cursor overlay and acks; executor proceeds after ack or timeout. Active state toggles a tab badge and keeps the capture surface alive.

verevon.gap: Only an AI rationale bubble and step badges; no cursor or element highlight overlay in BrowserChrome.
verevon.strengths: Live frames (SSE/WS) and typed step events already stream to the UI (v-quarry-141), so the data path exists.

clusters.benefit: Users can follow and trust what the AI is doing in the shared browser; strongly visible polish for co-browsing.
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane: include target box/point in step 'started' events; Frontend Plane: render an animated cursor and target highlight over the live frame (Solid overlay, reduced-motion aware). No ack needed server-side; keep it presentation-only.
clusters.risks: Overlay mis-alignment with scaled live frames; ZDR: coordinates are not sensitive.
clusters.rationale: High user visibility, moderate effort; follows co-browsing.

clusters.name: Run control protocol: steer, queue follow-ups, interrupt, replayable event stream
clusters.description: Clients drive a run over a versioned protocol with idempotent command ids and sequence-numbered events; users can steer a running turn, queue follow-ups or interrupt, and reconnecting clients resume from a sequence number.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: WS envelopes {op: command|ack|event|error, protocolVersion}, commands prompt/continue/steer{interrupt, expectedTurnId}/queue/abort, afterSeq resume.

clusters.mechanism: Command {id (idempotency), type, expectedTurnId}; server acks then emits events with monotonically increasing seq persisted per run; steer injects a user message at the next step boundary (optionally interrupting the in-flight step); queue appends to the run's inbox.

verevon.gap: Quarry has typed event SSE with ?from_seq replay and the gateway exposes pause/resume/stop, but the AI-loop wiring is likely broken (401/403) and no mid-run steering or queued follow-up for browser runs was found.
verevon.strengths: Durable, replayable typed event stream already exists in Quarry.

clusters.benefit: Users can redirect a browser agent without restarting it ('no, the second result'), a daily-use expectation.
clusters.approach: Model Plane: add steer/queue commands to browser_run (execution-core picks them up at step boundaries) with idempotency keys; reuse Quarry seq replay for the UI.
clusters.risks: Steering mid-action must not bypass pending approvals.
clusters.rationale: Noticeable UX gain once the loop runs.

clusters.name: Crash-safe runs: recovery, persistent suspensions and rerun-safe tool classification
clusters.description: If the agent host restarts, interrupted runs resume, runs waiting on a human stay suspended and continue when the decision arrives, and only tools marked rerun-safe are re-executed automatically.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: recoverInterruptedRuns per account, persisted suspensions, and an explicit CRASH_RERUN_SAFE_TOOLS allowlist with an 'unsettled tool result' message for others.

clusters.mechanism: Persist run/turn/tool-call state; on boot, resume runs in 'running' state; for an in-flight tool call, re-run only if in the rerun-safe set, else return an 'unsettled' result telling the model the outcome is unknown and to re-observe.

verevon.gap: Check that resume treats an in-flight non-idempotent action (submit, click) as 'unsettled' rather than replaying it. ZDR runs have no resume by design.
verevon.strengths: Immutable step receipts, checkpoints and resume with Postgres queue.

clusters.approach: Keep; add an explicit rerun-safe classification per AgentAction if missing.
clusters.rationale: Verevon is equal or ahead (durable receipts).

clusters.name: Durable human-in-the-loop approvals with fail-closed semantics
clusters.description: When an action needs a human, the run suspends with a persisted request that survives restarts and can be answered from any client; if approval cannot be obtained (no channel, timeout, cancelled) the action is blocked; headless runs auto-deny every 'ask'; paid tool calls can require approval up to a call budget.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: Aside persists suspensions that resume the exact tool call after a restart; Codex makes 'no explicit decision' fail closed and tells the model so. Firecrawl FA101 shows the API form (requireApproval with maxCalls).

clusters.mechanism: suspend(kind, toolCallId, request) writes {kind, request, createdAt} and status 'suspended'; any client resolves it; resolution resumes the identical frozen tool call. Missing elicitation channel, cancel or timeout => typed approval_unavailable/failed_closed, never implicit allow; headless sessions map ask->deny.

verevon.gap: Check headless/scheduled runs map 'ask' to deny rather than hanging.
verevon.strengths: Risk-classified approvals reuse generic orchestration approvals and fail closed; Quarry one-shot grants are scoped to exact frame/dialog/artifact and reject replay.

clusters.approach: Keep.
clusters.rationale: Equal to the references.

clusters.name: Risk-tier confirmation taxonomy and final-confirm mode with typed review artifacts
clusters.description: Browser actions are classified (hand-off required, always confirm, pre-approvable, no confirmation); an optional 'ask first' mode makes the agent pause before sending, posting, paying, deleting or final submissions and show a typed draft preview.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: request_action_confirmation must be the only tool call in the turn and carries a typed draft artifact (email, message, calendar event) for review; Codex CA034/CI105 provide the clearest taxonomy (DOC).

clusters.mechanism: Classifier maps (action, target, page context) to tier; tier>=confirm suspends with {title, message, artifact{type, fields}}; UI renders the draft; approval resumes exactly that action.

verevon.gap: Risk classes (login, checkout, posting_form, destructive, cross-domain, persistent cookie) are shipped; typed draft previews and a per-session 'ask first' switch are unverified.
verevon.strengths: Fail-closed, code-enforced classification (not prompt-only like part of Codex's DOC taxonomy).

clusters.approach: Keep; optionally add typed draft previews to approval cards.
clusters.rationale: Verevon's code-enforced risk gates are on par.

clusters.name: Automated safety reviewer model ('guardian') for approvals and sensitive actions
clusters.description: An independent reviewer model can approve or deny first-time origin access, every page-defined (WebMCP) tool call, credential prompts and sensitive submissions, using a bounded transcript slice and its own page capture; evidence shown to it is fenced as untrusted; approvals are cached briefly per thread and origin.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: guardian v2 cache keyed {threadId, origin} with 5-minute expiry, strict auto-review for credential prompts with a rubric comparing top-level origin and credential recipient, and explicit evidence fencing.

clusters.mechanism: Approval request -> reviewer sub-agent with {action, origin, sanitized URL, bounded transcript, reviewer-only page capture}; reviewer returns allow|deny|escalate; deny and escalate fail closed or go to the user; cache allow for (thread, origin) with short TTL; never treat missing evidence as permission.

verevon.gap: No safety reviewer for browser approvals was found (grep for auto_review/guardian: none). capability-core's llmreviewer is a skill-learning reviewer, not a safety gate. All 'ask' decisions go to the user.

clusters.benefit: Cuts approval fatigue for low-risk first-visit domains while keeping a fail-closed second opinion; useful for unattended (scheduled) runs where no human is present.
clusters.approach: Model Plane: optional reviewer step inside the approval pipeline (separate model call with a fixed rubric, no tools), allowed only for tiers marked pre-approvable; never for hand-off or always-confirm tiers; log reviewer decisions in receipts.
clusters.risks: Reviewer can itself be prompt-injected; must see fenced evidence only and never be the sole gate for irreversible actions. Cost per approval.
clusters.rationale: Useful later; human approvals are sufficient for the first release.

clusters.name: Session permission modes and rule engine with browser action classes
clusters.description: Every session runs in read-only, guard (default) or full-access mode; ordered rules decide allow/ask/deny for tools (name/glob + argument matchers), browser actions classed as read/modify/download with URL globs, and network access; policy is implemented as hooks wrapping every tool; unattended runs can be stricter. Aside also lets the agent rewrite its own permissions (AA070, an anti-pattern).

bestInClass.why: q5/q4 SRC: zod-typed modes and ordered rules, with every Page method declaring its action class and calling ensureAccess(action, url).

clusters.mechanism: Each executor method declares class read|modify|download; a central check evaluates rules in order deny > ask > allow > default for (mode, class, url glob, tool args); read-only mode denies modify/download outright.

verevon.gap: Broker grants carry domain allowlist, TTL and org/owner scope, and risk gates exist, but there is no explicit read-only/guard/full-access run mode and no per-action-class rules (e.g. 'read-only research run cannot type or submit'). Check whether grants can restrict action kinds.
verevon.strengths: Permissions live in a separate broker the model cannot write to (avoids Aside's AA070 self-modification risk).

clusters.benefit: Lets users and orgs launch 'read-only research' browser runs safely and scheduled runs with stricter policy; clean mapping onto broker grants.
clusters.approach: Model Plane (BrowserBroker): add mode and allowed action classes to the grant; Quarry classifies each AgentAction as read/modify/download/sensitive and rejects classes not in the grant.
clusters.risks: Never let the agent change its own mode; mode changes are user/Control Plane actions.
clusters.rationale: Natural extension of the grant model; enables safe read-only agents.

clusters.name: Single policy choke point with typed, non-retryable denials and anti-circumvention guidance
clusters.description: Every command touching a page is vetted against the tab's current URL before it runs; refusals carry a machine-readable reason, the deciding source (user, enterprise, reviewer, site status) and a retryable flag, and tell the model not to reach the same outcome through workarounds.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: runCommand -> ensureCommandAllowed for all non-exempt commands; 16-reason denial catalogue with decisionSource and retryable.

clusters.mechanism: Wrap the executor dispatch in one function: classify command (none|targetUrl|currentTab), evaluate policy, on deny return {code, decisionSource, retryable, message + fixed anti-circumvention sentence}.

verevon.gap: quarry-edge already validates the grant and domain per action (a choke point), but denials are generic QuarryError codes without decisionSource/retryable or anti-circumvention text, so the planner cannot tell 'retry later' from 'never'.
verevon.strengths: Per-action grant validation in the executor.

clusters.benefit: Fewer wasted retries and less model 'creativity' around denials; better audit.
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane: add {decision_source, retryable} to QuarryError for policy denials; Model Plane: render a standard anti-circumvention line in tool results.
clusters.risks: Low.
clusters.rationale: Small change with clear agent-behaviour benefit.

clusters.name: Per-origin consent with scoped persistence and deny-first resolution
clusters.description: First access to a new origin asks the user; the answer can be remembered for the turn, the conversation or globally (unless org policy forbids persistence); saved and enterprise denials always beat approvals, resolved from the narrowest scope up. Consent is per action class (browse, upload, download, raw CDP, site tools).

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: explicit resolution order (conversation deny, global deny, enterprise deny, turn cache, reviewer cache, saved approvals) and per-class consent.

clusters.mechanism: On navigation to origin O for class K: check denies (conversation, global, org) -> approvals (turn, conversation, global) -> prompt user with scope choices; store decision in a scoped table; org flag can forbid global persistence.

verevon.gap: Verevon enforces a fixed run-level domain allowlist from the grant (exact host or subdomain, pre/post action). There is no interactive 'allow this new origin?' prompt mid-run, no scoped persistence, and no per-class origin consent; an agent that needs a new domain fails instead of asking.
verevon.strengths: Fixed allowlists are strict and fail closed.

clusters.benefit: Makes open-ended browsing tasks possible without pre-declaring every domain, while keeping explicit user consent and owner-plane authority (new domain = new child grant).
clusters.approach: Model Plane: on Quarry 'domain not in grant' denial, raise a consent approval; on approval BrowserBroker issues a child grant adding the origin for the chosen scope (run, conversation, user default), stored in the broker; deny wins; org policy (C29) caps it.
clusters.risks: Consent fatigue; persistence must be per user/org and never widen Space ACLs.
clusters.rationale: Needed for useful general browsing, builds on existing grants.

clusters.name: Org/enterprise origin policy with wildcard pattern language and deny-wins merge
clusters.description: Admins set per-origin policy for access, uploads, downloads, raw CDP, auto-review and persistent approvals; a precise pattern language ('*.x' subdomains only, '**.x' apex plus subdomains); denial from either admin or user config wins. Firecrawl constrains agent runs to supplied URLs with threat-protection checks; Aside ships no allow/deny list by default (AA071, INF).

bestInClass.why: q5/q4 SRC: field-level deny-wins merge across admin and user config; IPv6 and trailing-dot normalisation in patterns.

clusters.mechanism: Policy = {defaultOriginPolicy, origins[pattern] -> {access, uploads, downloads, rawCdp, autoReview, persist}}; normalise host (lowercase, strip trailing dot, IPv6 brackets); match exact > '*.' > '**.'; merge admin and user per field with deny precedence.

verevon.gap: Domain allowlist supports exact host or subdomain; no org-admin per-origin policy (block lists, per-class rules) was identified in the baseline. Check Control Plane for an org browser policy object.
verevon.strengths: Broker policy is authoritative when grants are required.

clusters.benefit: Enterprise customers expect admin block/allow lists (no banking, no personal mail) applied to all agents.
clusters.approach: Control Plane owns the org policy object; BrowserBroker reads it when issuing grants and intersects it with user consent (deny wins); Quarry enforces only what is in the grant (no cross-plane DB access).
clusters.risks: Policy drift between Control and Model Plane caches; version the policy in the grant.
clusters.rationale: Enterprise requirement; reuses existing grant flow.

clusters.name: Navigation guard: scheme allowlist and request-level interception of redirects, subframes and popups
clusters.description: While the agent controls a tab only http(s) and about:blank are allowed; disallowed navigations, including page-initiated redirects, subframes and window.open, are cancelled at request level; main-document responses can be paused for vetting; certificate-error interstitials require hand-off.

bestInClass.why: q5/q4 SRC: shell-level restriction covers redirects, subframes and popups; fail-closed interceptors.

clusters.mechanism: Enable request interception for all requests; on each paused request evaluate scheme + origin policy; fail the request on deny and emit a navigationBlocked event; missing policy = deny all.

verevon.gap: Certificate-interstitial handling not verified.
verevon.strengths: Quarry installs a fail-closed CDP Fetch guard before navigation that covers redirects, frames, XHR and subresources with deny-all default, and allows only http/https (SRC, read in this audit): equal to Codex.

clusters.approach: Keep; add explicit cert-error detection that maps to a hand-off.
clusters.rationale: Verevon equals Codex here.

clusters.name: Site reputation gate before navigation
clusters.description: Before visiting a site the runtime asks a reputation service whether browsing agents are permitted there; blocked sites are refused without prompting; results cached; fail-open only on transport errors (Codex).

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC: server-side site_status endpoint keyed by origin+path with conversation/turn ids, cached per origin.

clusters.mechanism: Before navigate: lookup(origin, path) in a reputation cache; on miss call the reputation service; deny if blocked category (malware, phishing, disallowed agent use).

verevon.gap: Only a capability flag 'cap.self_owned.quarry_url_reputation_feeds' exists in capability-core; no reputation lookup was found in Quarry crates (SRC grep).

clusters.benefit: Protects agents and users from phishing/malware pages and prompt-injection farms; supports enterprise compliance.
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane: add a reputation check in the egress policy (feeds such as Safe Browsing-style lists cached locally) evaluated alongside the domain grant; deny with decision_source=site_status.
clusters.risks: Privacy: do not send full URLs of ZDR sessions to third-party services; prefer local hashed-prefix lists.
clusters.rationale: Domain grants already limit exposure; reputation is defence in depth.

clusters.name: Escape-hatch gating: raw CDP and JavaScript evaluation
clusters.description: Raw DevTools access is off by default, needs per-origin high-risk consent plus enterprise permission and is filtered to an allowlist of CDP domains with a method denylist and URL-explicit parameters; page JavaScript may only be evaluated read-only in an isolated world that hides credential fields.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: three gates plus a 22-domain allowlist, URL-authorising cookie/request params, and a read-only evaluate wrapper that cannot mutate the DOM.

clusters.mechanism: Evaluate in Page.createIsolatedWorld with a frozen read-only proxy of document (no setters, no event dispatch), JSON-serializable args only, credential inputs masked; raw CDP only when the grant has rawCdp=true and method in allowlist.

verevon.gap: The Verevon UI facade blocks raw script, but Quarry's AgentAction::Evaluate and raw CSS actions are available on normal agent runs without per-action approval (baseline flags it as a risk). A model-proposed Evaluate can mutate the page or read sensitive fields outside the risk gates.
verevon.strengths: UI facade already refuses raw script.

clusters.benefit: Closes a bypass of the risk-classified approval model: any risky action could be expressed as Evaluate.
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane: make Evaluate read-only by default (isolated world, no mutation, credential masking) and require an explicit grant capability plus one-shot approval for mutating script; Model Plane: hide Evaluate from the planner unless the grant allows it.
clusters.risks: Some extraction flows may rely on mutating evaluate; audit callers first.
clusters.rationale: Security gap in an executor that otherwise fails closed; small fix.

clusters.name: Gated uploads and downloads with one-time grants
clusters.description: Uploads only through the file-chooser event with per-origin approval; downloads only when initiated by an approved agent flow, with one-time grants tied to tab, session and exact URL (blob URLs bound to page origin), and unsolicited downloads cancelled; downloaded files are handed to the agent's workspace.

bestInClass.why: q5/q4 SRC: grant {grantedAtMs, sessionId, url} consumed in the will-download handler, URL-chain matched, expiring. Aside AA081 shows the handoff of the downloaded path into the sandbox.

clusters.mechanism: allowDownload(url) stores a one-time grant; the download handler consumes a matching grant (url or redirect chain, same tab/session, not expired) else cancels; uploads: wait for Page.fileChooserOpened (intercepted), check approval, DOM.setFileInputFiles with artifact paths.

verevon.gap: Quarry implements artifact-only upload/download and one-shot grants, but the driver capability is false so these actions are rejected.
verevon.strengths: One-shot grants scoped to exact artifact already exist.

clusters.benefit: Agents that research or file paperwork need PDFs/CSVs and form uploads; files land as Verevon artifacts/documents (Data Plane) rather than on a desktop.
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane: enable the capability, store downloads as Quarry artifacts with checksum and MIME sniffing, hand off to Data Plane via its API (no cross-plane DB); uploads only from artifacts the run's owner can read.
clusters.risks: Malware in downloads (scan), ACL widening on uploads (check owner-plane ACL), ZDR artifacts must be ephemeral.
clusters.rationale: Mostly built; flipping it on needs safety review.

clusters.name: Secure credential handoff: the model never sees secrets
clusters.description: For sign-in the agent submits only selectors and labels; the host shows a secure form or saved-login picker, fills the fields itself in an isolated world and returns only a status; after delivery the agent is blocked from observing that document until a new one loads; OTP, QR and number-matching flows; Aside offers opaque vault references and fill-by-ref.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: request validation against the live page, native isolated-world delivery, an observation-gate state machine that blocks AX/DOM/screenshot reads after delivery, and machine-readable recovery steps. Aside AB061 (q5) adds password-reference fill without a UI form.

clusters.mechanism: Agent: browserAuth.request({origin, fields[{label, selector, autocomplete}], submit}). Runtime validates origin and selector uniqueness/visibility; UI renders a secure form (or vault picker); values go executor -> CDP isolated world -> input.value + input events; agent receives {status}. Mark document as credential-delivered; deny observations of that loader id until navigation; errors include next-step codes.

verevon.gap: No secret references in AgentAction or quarry-edge; sensitive-data redaction is a stub without callers. Today a login would require the model to type secrets (or the user to take over).

clusters.benefit: Logged-in sites are where agents create most value; doing it without exposing secrets to the model, logs or receipts is a hard requirement for ZDR and enterprise trust.
clusters.approach: Control Plane: secret store with opaque references scoped to user/org; Frontend: secure credential form outside the live frame; Ingestion Plane: fill_secret{ref, selector} action executed in an isolated world, observation gate on that document, redaction of receipts/frames; Model Plane: only sees ref ids and status.
clusters.risks: Live frames/screenshots can leak typed secrets: blank or blur credential fields in frames and block observations until navigation; never log values.
clusters.rationale: Blocks the main agent use cases on authenticated sites; references converge on the same design.

clusters.name: Payment and spending consent policy
clusters.description: Users configure whether the agent may pay (ask, auto-approve under a USD limit, never), which cards, per-card notes and daily/monthly limits; Aside's enforcement path was not observed (AA058).

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: settings schema with thresholds, cards and spending limits.

clusters.mechanism: Settings {paymentUse.enabled, beforePaying ask|auto-under|never, autoApproveUnderUsd, cards[], spendingLimits}; checkout actions are classified and gated against limits.

verevon.gap: Checkout is a risk class that always requires approval; there is no card or spending policy.
verevon.strengths: Checkout always needs explicit approval (safer default).

clusters.benefit: Low for now; autonomous payment is high-risk and not core to Verevon's workspace vision.
clusters.approach: Do not build now; keep checkout as always-confirm. Revisit with Control Plane billing/policy if customers ask.
clusters.risks: Financial loss and fraud liability.
clusters.rationale: Out of scope and risky; existing always-confirm gate is the right default.

clusters.name: Prompt-injection guard for web content
clusters.description: Tool/page output is wrapped in explicit untrusted-data boundaries with fake boundaries and role tags neutralised (Aside, tiered by model capability); Codex states the policy that web content never grants permission; Firecrawl offers an opt-in classifier check on scraped content that aborts with a typed error.

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC: concrete neutralisation of role tags (including spaced spellings) and fake boundaries plus envelopes; Firecrawl FE097 (q4) adds chunked classifier screening (32k chunks, 2k overlap) for API users.

clusters.mechanism: Before returning page text to the model: neutralise strings resembling role tags/boundaries, wrap in BEGIN/END UNTRUSTED markers with a fixed warning; optionally classify chunks with a small model and block or flag.

verevon.gap: Model Plane screens ExternalWeb/BrowserScraped/ThirdPartyMcp results unconditionally (shipped). Quarry itself has no injection labelling/detection in the observation path, so direct Quarry API consumers (scrape/extract) get no guard like Firecrawl's checkPromptInjection.
verevon.strengths: Unconditional provenance-based screening in execution-core.

clusters.benefit: Consistent protection for every consumer of Quarry content, not only the Model Plane agent path.
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane: add an opt-in prompt-injection flag on scrape/extract that labels suspicious spans and can fail with a typed error; keep the Model Plane screening authoritative for agents.
clusters.risks: False positives; classifier cost; fail-open billing semantics need a decision.
clusters.rationale: Agent path is already guarded; this is for API consumers.

clusters.name: Site-specific playbooks and per-site instructions
clusters.description: Built-in playbooks for popular apps (canonical URLs, scoped selectors, rules) injected by URL or keyword; server-supplied per-site guidance in page observations that grants no extra permission.

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC: sixteen playbooks as SKILL.md files with autoInject {keywords, url} frontmatter.

clusters.mechanism: Skill registry keyed by URL pattern/keywords; on navigation or task match, inject the playbook text into the next observation header; mark it as guidance only.

verevon.gap: Unknown: check whether Model Plane skills (capability-core learning/skills) can be bound to URL patterns for browser runs.

clusters.benefit: Higher success on common SaaS UIs; Verevon's skill-learning pipeline could generate them from successful runs (procedure compile, C42).
clusters.approach: Model Plane: URL-pattern-bound skills injected into browser observations; seed with a few top sites; learn more from receipts.
clusters.risks: Stale selectors; playbooks must never grant permissions.
clusters.rationale: Incremental quality gain after the loop works.

clusters.name: Session-cookie API calls and site API globals instead of UI driving
clusters.description: The agent issues fetches that reuse the page's cookies and user agent, and calls site APIs (LinkedIn, Gmail, Docs, Notion, X, YouTube transcripts) directly with the browser session.

bestInClass.why: q3 SRC: cookie-carrying Node fetch behind a network permission hook plus per-site API clients.

clusters.mechanism: Network.getCookies(url) from the active tab -> set Cookie and User-Agent headers -> fetch, gated by a network permission rule.

verevon.gap: Unknown (no baseline record). Verevon's Integration Plane provider actions cover the 'API instead of UI' need with proper OAuth scopes.
verevon.strengths: Integration Plane connectors are the sanctioned path.

clusters.benefit: Low: replaying browser cookies against private APIs bypasses provider consent and ToS and is fragile.
clusters.approach: Do not build; route to Integration Plane connectors (C08).
clusters.risks: ToS violations, session theft blast radius, ACL widening.
clusters.rationale: Conflicts with Verevon's authority model; connectors are the right tool.

clusters.name: Subagents with isolated browser state and read-only side chats
clusters.description: The main agent spawns bounded background subagents with their own tabs and REPL, no access to the parent's tabs, and some read-only profiles; users can open a side chat that reads but does not drive the main task.

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC: up to 8 subagents with profiles (context_explorer read-only, code_explorer) and prompt-cache fork.

clusters.mechanism: subagent.spawn(profile, task) -> new session with its own browser binding and tool set filtered by profile; parent waits via subagent_wait; results returned as text.

verevon.gap: Quarry supports parallel runs; whether execution-core can fan out browser subagents with separate grants is unverified.
verevon.strengths: Multi-run parallelism in Quarry.

clusters.benefit: Parallel research across sites; fits Model Plane agents.
clusters.approach: Model Plane: allow a run to spawn child browser runs with child grants (narrower domains, read-only class) and aggregate results.
clusters.risks: Cost explosion; cap concurrency per org.
clusters.rationale: Useful for research tasks, not core.

clusters.name: Remote and external drivers of the browser runtime
clusters.description: A user's desktop browser can be driven and approved from another device via an outbound relay; external agents (coding agents) can drive the same browser tools through a CLI with an ephemeral session; cloud agents can use the local browser only with a signed access attestation.

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC: outbound-only relay with an allow-listed set of remote operations; Codex CI109 adds signed browser-access attestation for cloud agents.

clusters.mechanism: Host enrolls with a relay and keeps an outbound WebSocket; remote clients can only call an allowlisted set of session operations; external CLI gets its own incognito-style session under the same permission engine.

verevon.gap: Quarry is a server-side service, so any authorised device can drive sessions; exposing Quarry browser control to external agents (e.g. via MCP) with broker grants is not evidenced.
verevon.strengths: Cloud-native: no relay needed and cookies never live on a single desktop.

clusters.benefit: Lets external coding/automation agents use Verevon's governed browser.
clusters.approach: Model Plane: expose browser.observe/act as an MCP tool behind the same broker grants and approvals.
clusters.risks: External clients must not obtain grants outside the user's ACL.
clusters.rationale: Architecture already covers the remote case; MCP exposure is optional.

clusters.name: Visual proof and recording of agent work
clusters.description: Tasks end with visual proof (fresh locator screenshot), optional screenshot on every snapshot, screen recording of the agent tab as video, and attaching window screenshots plus accessibility text to chat.

bestInClass.why: q3 SRC: mandatory final proof screenshot and screencast-to-ffmpeg video artifacts.

clusters.mechanism: Page.startScreencast frames piped to an encoder with timestamps; final proof = element screenshot of the confirming element.

verevon.gap: No video recording artifact; immutable receipts and proof bundles cover evidence.
verevon.strengths: Proof bundle, immutable step receipts, browser timeline and live frames exceed both references' evidence model.

clusters.approach: Keep; optional video export from live frames for non-ZDR runs.
clusters.rationale: Verevon ahead on auditable evidence.

clusters.name: Task record and replay of browser procedures
clusters.description: Codex has feature flags for record-and-replay but no browser replay mechanism was observed (INF, low confidence). (Supported only by DOC/INF records.)

bestInClass.why: Only reference; INF q2, gated and not observed in the browser path.

clusters.mechanism: Not established in references. Verevon: compile a successful run's receipts into a parameterised procedure and replay-check it.

verevon.gap: Quarry compiles procedures and runs replay/quality/impact checks, but has no procedure store or execute endpoint and Verevon does not call them.
verevon.strengths: Verevon is ahead of all references here (procedure compile and replay checks exist in code).

clusters.approach: Keep and finish: procedure store plus execute endpoint, then wire to the UI ('save as routine').
clusters.rationale: Verevon ahead; reference support is INF only.

clusters.name: WebMCP site tools: page-defined agent tools
clusters.description: Pages that register tools through Chromium's document.modelContext are discovered per tab/frame and offered to the agent as callable tools instead of clicking, with per-site settings and strict review of each call.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: CDP WebMCP.enable on every frame target, toolsAdded/Removed events, handles bound to registration ids.

clusters.mechanism: Enable the WebMCP CDP domain per frame; maintain a per-tab tool registry; expose tools as 'webmcp:<host>:<tool>' with schemas; each invocation requires per-site permission and review.

verevon.gap: No modelContext/WebMCP handling found in Quarry crates (SRC grep).

clusters.benefit: Emerging standard: when sites adopt it, agents get reliable typed actions instead of UI driving.
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane: discover WebMCP tools in observations; Model Plane proposes calls; Quarry executes with one-shot approval per call (sensitive class).
clusters.risks: Page-defined tools are untrusted input; descriptions must be fenced.
clusters.rationale: Low adoption today; track the standard.

clusters.name: Bot-detection and CAPTCHA reporting with strict no-bypass scope
clusters.description: The agent reports why a site blocked it (captcha failed, access denied, challenge loop) as telemetry recording only the hostname, and never bypasses challenges.

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC: typed report reasons with careful exclusions (bare 403, admin blocks).

clusters.mechanism: Classify challenge signals in observation; emit typed telemetry; hand off to the user.

verevon.gap: Ensure challenge signals map to a user hand-off (C19).
verevon.strengths: Challenge signals are part of every observation.

clusters.approach: Keep.
clusters.rationale: Equal.

clusters.name: Web notifications and push as agent triggers
clusters.description: The agent silently grants a site an 'Allow for AI' notification permission and wakes a routine when the site pushes a notification.

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC: permission grant plus routine trigger.

clusters.mechanism: Grant notifications for origin; route push events to a routine scheduler.

verevon.gap: Unknown (no baseline); Verevon has Application Plane notifications but no web-push-triggered browser routines evidenced.

clusters.benefit: Low: server-side sessions are not long-lived user browsers; triggers belong in the Integration Plane (webhooks).
clusters.approach: Do not build; use Integration Plane webhooks/polling for triggers.
clusters.risks: Silent permission grants conflict with explicit consent.
clusters.rationale: Does not fit server-side browser sessions.

clusters.name: Background task UX and proactive suggestions
clusters.description: Agents run in the background with a task list, attention/completion notifications and sounds; a proactive mode searches user context with minimal questions; suggested tasks from draft routines appear in onboarding.

bestInClass.why: q3 SRC: needs-attention and completion notifications, approvals reachable from notifications.

clusters.mechanism: Run state changes (needs_approval, completed, failed) publish notifications; UI task list subscribes.

verevon.gap: Unknown: check Application Plane notifications for browser-run events (needs approval, completed).

clusters.benefit: Users can leave a browser run in the background and return when approval is needed.
clusters.approach: Application Plane: subscribe to Quarry/Model run events and emit notifications; skip proactive history mining.
clusters.risks: Notification noise.
clusters.rationale: Cheap once run events flow.

clusters.name: Gated access to the user's browsing context (history, session stores)
clusters.description: History can be read only after approval with bounded queries; browser discovery must never inspect cookies, local storage, profiles or passwords.

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC: approval, small query budget, date bounds, policy kill switch.

clusters.mechanism: history.search({query, from, to}) behind an approval and a per-turn budget.

verevon.gap: Not applicable to server-side Quarry sessions (no user history). Principle applies to persistent profiles: agents must not read profile cookie stores directly.

clusters.benefit: Low.
clusters.approach: No build; keep persistent profiles opaque to the model.
clusters.rationale: No user browsing history in Verevon's model.

clusters.name: Desktop computer use over native apps and windows
clusters.description: A unified API to observe and act on native applications and windows (UI Automation, SendInput, occluded-window capture), via a native helper with turn scoping and request budgets; Aside's Windows helper captures context only.

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC: same observe/act surface for apps and browsers, native helper with budgets and respawn.

clusters.mechanism: Native helper process over NDJSON; window objects from enumeration only; AX state + screenshot; input via SendInput after activation.

verevon.gap: Verevon has no desktop agent; Model Plane sandboxes are server-side.

clusters.benefit: None for a web/cloud product.
clusters.approach: Do not build.
clusters.risks: Large security surface on user machines.
clusters.rationale: Out of scope for Verevon's web-first architecture.

clusters.name: Desktop computer-use safety controls (per-app approval, forbidden classes, managed policy, kill switch)
clusters.description: Per-app approval negotiated by the helper, refusal of password managers/security software/terminals, enterprise app policy bound to signed package identity, URL policy when the target window is a browser, and a physical Escape-key kill switch per turn.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: physical kill switch with a per-turn interrupt marker; per-app approvals.

clusters.mechanism: Helper exits on Escape and writes a marker; later calls in that turn are refused.

verevon.gap: Not applicable (no desktop agent). The per-turn kill-switch idea maps to C19 (enforced takeover epoch).

clusters.benefit: None directly.
clusters.approach: Do not build; reuse the kill-switch concept in C19.
clusters.rationale: Tied to desktop computer use.

clusters.name: Agent control of embedded MCP App widgets
clusters.description: The agent can inspect and operate MCP App UIs shown in side-panel tabs but cannot create or navigate tabs.

bestInClass.why: Only reference (q4 SRC).

clusters.mechanism: A backend that maps tab commands to the MCP App iframe with navigation disabled.

verevon.gap: Unknown whether Verevon renders MCP Apps at all.

clusters.benefit: Low.
clusters.approach: Revisit only if Verevon adopts MCP Apps.
clusters.rationale: No MCP Apps surface in Verevon evidenced.

clusters.name: Prompt-driven multi-step browser agent run (planner loop)
clusters.description: A model-driven loop observes the page (AX refs), chooses an action, executes and re-observes until done, exposed as a hosted 'interact with this page by prompt' API (Firecrawl) or as the browser agent harness (Aside v1 harness).

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC: concise hosted design: initial interactive snapshot (capped 40k chars), a single tool issuing agent-browser commands with @eN refs, guardrails and step caps inside the sandbox. Aside AA035 shows harness versioning.

clusters.mechanism: Loop: snapshot -i (interactive refs, capped) + URL -> LLM with one tool (browser command) -> execute -> new snapshot diff -> stop on done/step cap/budget; guardrails reject commands outside the allowed set.

verevon.gap: Durable loop with pause/resume/stop and an LLM planner exist in execution-core, but the LLM planner is gated by QUARRY_BROWSER_AGENT_LLM (not set in compose), so the default loop is deterministic observe; gateway calls likely fail auth (see C01); Quarry's own planner is an unused stub by design.
verevon.strengths: Planning correctly lives in the Model Plane; Quarry only executes.

clusters.benefit: This is the AI-browser feature users see; without an enabled planner the in-app browser has no real agent.
clusters.approach: Model Plane: enable the LLM planner by default behind org policy, add step/budget caps and the procedure prompt (C07), integrate risk gates and ZDR checks already present; Frontend: one entry point 'Do this in the browser'.
clusters.risks: Cost and runaway loops: enforce step/time/token budgets per run.
clusters.rationale: Core product vision; most code exists but is disabled or unreachable.
